Use case: ads-marketing
Asset type: social-system for an AYESMAJ portfolio case study
Primary request: Create one cohesive social campaign system with six distinct tiles: hero, product or service proof, detail, atmosphere, announcement-style composition, and closing brand moment. Every tile must share one art direction.
Brand: GENERAL WORK
Category: Mixed Media
Brand character: A selection of creative work spanning photography, digital art, and experimental visuals that don't fit neatly into a single category.
Input images: Image 1: source-of-truth brand reference (3.png); Image 2: source-of-truth brand reference (2.png); Image 3: source-of-truth brand reference (5.png)
Scene/backdrop: extend only the world established by the reference images; do not import unrelated motifs
Style/medium: premium cinematic advertising, polished editorial design, photoreal materials, credible production value
Composition/framing: 16:9 premium social-grid presentation with six clean frames, controlled variety, and a strong central rhythm; underlying brand composition language: curated AYESMAJ experimental-gallery rhythm with intentional contrast
Lighting/mood: polished studio light adapted to each featured artwork
Color palette: #000000, #120000, #230301, #12191B, #385468, #5F95B7, #070000
Materials/textures: glass, gloss packaging, cinematic print, CGI surfaces
Constraints: Treat every input as immutable source-of-truth. Preserve the real product category, recognizable product geometry, packaging architecture, palette, logo placement logic, and personality. Create a meaningful new portfolio touchpoint, not a duplicate of a reference. No unsupported SKU, feature, metric, certification, client result, or commercial claim.
Text constraints: Do not generate readable paragraphs, slogans, prices, specifications, legal copy, or invented brand spelling. Use abstract typographic blocks where interface text is needed. If a real logo is visible on a referenced physical product, preserve its placement and appearance; never create an alternate logo.
Avoid: generic AI filler, unrelated sci-fi objects, excessive particles, visual clutter, warped products, duplicate objects, malformed hands or faces, fake labels, watermarks, third-party logos, and brand drift.
